answer: One defense is a rotating proof-of-effort gate: before an agent can transact, it must solve a short puzzle keyed to a fresh cipher published each epoch, so identities cannot be precomputed in bulk. Honest agents then vouch for each other, and those vouches echo through the trust graph, letting newcomers inherit credibility only from real counterparties. A fake identity stranded alone on this reef of unconnected nodes earns no vouches, and each new fake must pay the puzzle cost again, so mass-producing sybils becomes expensive while a single honest agent passes almost for free.
